key_insight: A high-order FR/CPR solver coupled with a rotating actuator-line model can predict VAWT aerodynamics on fixed Cartesian grids without resolving blade geometry, while still capturing unsteady wake and stall physics.
engineering_relevance: This provides a geometry-free, computationally efficient tool for turbine design studies, mesh-convergence screening, and large-scale wind-energy simulations.
method: Couples FR/CPR flow solver with rotating actuator-line model (ALM)
Uses isotropic Gaussian kernel to project blade forces in a blade-attached frame
Adds modified Boeing-Vertol dynamic stall model and DMST correction for inflow on coarse meshes
evidence_signal: Validated against experimental near-wake data and prior LES-ALM results, with mean wake profiles in good agreement and power-coefficient predictions within 6% of high-fidelity 3D LES-ALM near optimal operating conditions.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on proper Gaussian-kernel resolution and coarse-mesh induction treatment; without the mesh criterion and DMST correction, physical inflow and loading can be underpredicted.
paper_title: A High-Order Flux Reconstruction Actuator-Line Framework for Rotating-Blade Aerodynamics on Fixed Cartesian Grids
